input.quote: 22.1 Governing Law. The validity, construction and interpretation of this Agreement and the rights and duties of the parties hereto shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of Wisconsin, excluding its principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 selects Wisconsin internal law and Section 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in the courts of Milwaukee County and the Eastern District of Wisconsin. Wisconsin is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback governing-law and forum elements on their material terms. It is not walk-away territory: dispute resolution is before courts, Article 15 provides only a non-binding executive escalation (no mandatory arbitration, and the arbitration references in 22.2 and 22.11 are incidental), and the venue is a domestic forum. We therefore replaced only the jurisdiction and forum words with the preferred New York position, leaving the conflict-of-laws exclusion, the judgment-enforcement sentence and all other wording intact. Delaware or California law and courts remain an acceptable fallback.

proposal.summary: Move governing law and exclusive venue from Wisconsin to New York law and the New York County courts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law from Wisconsin to New York and set exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, our accepted position; Delaware or California courts are an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: the internal laws of the State of Wisconsin
ops.newText: the internal laws of the State of New York

ops.oldText: the parties consent to venue in an exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Milwaukee County, Wisconsin and the Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.
ops.newText: the parties consent to venue in and the exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of the state and federal courts in New York County, New York.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
